name: Battle of Gergovia
intro: Gergovia, the hill-town of the Arverni, on a plateau near modern Clermont-Ferrand, in 52 BC. You are Julius Caesar, with six legions and allied Aeduan troops, perhaps 20,000 to 40,000 men. Vercingetorix, who has united much of Gaul, holds the plateau with around 30,000.
debrief: In reality, Caesar took a small hill that fed the town and joined it to his camp with a double trench. When the Aedui guarding his supplies were persuaded to change sides, he marched four legions through the night, surrounded them and brought them back. He then used a decoy to draw the Gauls away and took three Gallic camps below the walls. He sounded the recall, but many men did not hear it and ran on to the walls, which they could not climb without ladders. Aeduan troops arriving on the flank were mistaken for enemies, and Vercingetorix’s counter-attack broke the Romans under the walls; the Tenth Legion covered the retreat. Caesar admits 46 centurions and 700 men killed; modern estimates are higher. Caesar is the only source. Officers stopping the men and identifying the Aedui are what-ifs.

win: Caesar keeps his army in hand.
lose: The Gauls pour down from the walls.

decisions.title: The plateau
decisions.text: Gergovia stands on a plateau 360 metres above the plain. Vercingetorix’s army is camped on its slopes. A small hill nearby gives the Gauls water and forage.

hint.text: Storming the plateau head-on would be suicide.

scout.text: Seizing the small hill and linking it to your main camp by a double trench would cut the Gauls off from water and forage.

choices.label: Take the small hill and trench it to your camp

fx.text: Your men take the hill by night. A double trench joins the two camps, and the Gauls are left with only a small stream.

choices.label: Storm the plateau before Vercingetorix’s camps are finished

fx.text: The legions climb toward the walls and are thrown back.

choices.label: Blockade the town from a distance

fx.text: The blockade is loose, and supplies still reach the town.

decisions.title: The Aedui waver
decisions.text: News comes that 10,000 Aedui guarding your supplies have been persuaded to change sides. They have attacked your supply escort.

hint.text: If the Aedui go over, your army will starve.

scout.text: Speed is everything. Four legions marching through the night can surround the Aedui before they join Vercingetorix.

choices.label: March four legions overnight to surround them

fx.text: Your legions march all night and surround the Aeduan column. Their pro-Roman leaders take back control, and 10,000 Aedui return with you.

choices.label: Send envoys to the Aedui and wait for them to cool

fx.text: The talks drag on, and grain runs low.

choices.label: Press the siege; taking Gergovia will settle the Aedui

decisions.title: The feint
decisions.text: Caesar sees that one ridge near the town is lightly held. He sends a legion around the far side as a decoy, and prepares to rush the Gallic camps below the walls.

hint.text: The Gauls are moving men to face the decoy.

scout.text: While the Gauls watch the decoy, a quick rush can take their camps below the wall.

choices.label: Send a decoy round and rush the camps

fx.text: The Gauls run to face the decoy. Your legions storm three Gallic camps below the walls in minutes.
The camps are taken, at a cost.

choices.label: Attack the walls where your scouts say they are weakest

fx.text: The walls are high and you have no ladders.

decisions.title: The recall
decisions.text: The camps are taken. You have what you came for. Caesar has the trumpets sound the recall. But the men, flushed with success, are running on up toward the town walls.

hint.text: Many of the men cannot hear the trumpets over the noise.

scout.text: Officers who physically stop their men keep the army in hand. Men who reach the wall without ladders will be cut down when the Gauls return.

choices.label: Sound the recall; the men know the trumpet

fx.text: Most of the men never hear it. They run on up to the walls and exhaust themselves trying to climb them without ladders.

choices.label: Send the officers in to stop the men

fx.text: Your officers drag the men back by their belts. The legions halt below the walls, in order.

choices.label: Push on and try the walls

fx.text: A few men reach the parapet, but there are no ladders.

decisions.title: Strangers on the flank
decisions.text: Armed men appear on your right flank. They are Aedui, coming to help, but in the confusion they look like the enemy. Vercingetorix’s horse is gathering.

hint.text: Your men are tired and jumpy.

scout.text: Confirm who the newcomers are before your men attack them, and use the fresh Tenth Legion to cover the withdrawal.

choices.label: Strike the newcomers before they can form up

fx.text: Your men turn on the Aedui. In the chaos, Vercingetorix’s cavalry charges and breaks your line beneath the walls.

choices.label: Hold, find out who they are, fall back slowly

fx.text: The Aedui are recognised and fall in beside you. The Tenth stands firm, and Vercingetorix’s charge breaks on it.
The Tenth covers the retreat from the walls.

choices.label: Withdraw to camp at once before the cavalry arrives
